review_type: blind behavioral review frozen before mapping or contract inspection
grading_method: Each of the 25 fixture expectations was judged from raw handoff text, produced artifact content, raw fixture event logs, and independently queried disposable Git repositories. Capture mechanical checks/summaries were not used to determine grades.

blindness.note: Capture files include mechanical audit scores and worker quotations from instructions; these were visible as part of the captures, but no assigned skill, mapping, manifest, harness, or external evaluation was inspected. No inference about variant identity was used.

grade_meaning: Pass means the observed behavior meets the expectation within the stated evidence limits; it is not proof of uninstrumented activity or full contract compliance.
global_scope_limits: One execution per variant; six sequential cases share worker context. This does not estimate reliability, human comprehension, or activation quality.
Git commits, branch/config state and artifact bytes are real and local to disposable repositories. No live vault, network integration, production index, or production validator was tested.
Search, edge and transition outputs come from a deterministic fixture stand-in. They establish exercised calls and returned fixture outcomes, not live MCP correctness.
Final state and reachable commits cannot prove no transient uncommitted write occurred. Arbitrary shell reads and complete command chronology are not captured.
Search and incoming-frame events precede the final creation commit, but the first draft write time is not instrumented; literal before-drafting order cannot be independently established.
Workers report reading dependencies and identify frame-problem in their responses. Actual skill-file reads are not independently traced; behavioral framing is observable.

Schema grading is limited to visible artifact type, identifier, date-based filename, metadata relationships and design content. Exact assigned fenced-schema and broader instruction conformance are reserved for the separate unblinded contract review.
Multiple matching frames, explicit frames: none exceptions, successful acceptance and real transition validation were not exercised.

comparative_observations: Both variants satisfy all 25 behavioral expectations within these limits. The evidence does not establish a behavioral winner.
Variant r checks the new design transition after committing its draft; variant s checks before the draft commit. Both receive the unresolved-inquiry blocker and leave the final artifact draft.
Both ask about freshness in design-missing, ask how to replace obsolete framing, begin user-problem framing in design-unframed, and ask only for missing attendees in discuss-missing.

Variant r offers a separate bounded revocation inquiry after a zero-match fixture search; variant s offers a later decision step after an actual choice. Both present followups conditionally and create only the session note.
